task.description: Close REVIEWER's 2 carried-forward coverage gaps (global_cap/1 non-default regression, permanent hardcoded-literal-regression for the 6 gated sweeps) and run a full independent AC-to-test traceability pass against ISS-0421's own remaining-in-scope acceptance properties (AC1 fault isolation, AC3 peak-DBConnection-checkouts arithmetic, AC4 single-query-per-tick), writing test/specs/ISS-0421.md and any new tests needed.

result.summary:
Wrote test/specs/ISS-0421.md documenting the full coverage map, and added 4 new tests total (2 in test/letflow/admission_test.exs, 3 describe blocks / 2 tests in test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs -- one describe holds 1 test, plus the AC1 and AC4 describes each holding 1 test, plus 3 tests in the global_cap/1 describe -- 5 new test cases total across the 2 files: 3 in admission_test.exs, 2 in poller_test.exs... corrected count: admission_test.exs gained 3 tests (one describe block), poller_test.exs gained 3 tests (three describe blocks: hardcoded-literal regression [1 test], AC1 rescue [1 test], AC4 single-query [1 test]). 6 new tests total.

1. CLOSED REVIEWER GAP 1 (global_cap/1 non-default regression): test/letflow/admission_test.exs, describe 'ISS-0421: global_cap/1 reads this instance's own live global_cap, not a default', 3 tests -- (a) pool_size:3/reserved_headroom:2 -> global_cap/1 == 1 (the exact REQ-218 test config), (b) a second, different non-default pair (12/2 -> 10) cross-checked against try_acquire(:global)'s own independently-implemented admission count (10 succeed, 11th rejected), (c) the documented default-config case (10/2 -> 8) for regression completeness.

2. CLOSED REVIEWER GAP 2 (permanent hardcoded-literal regression): test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs, describe 'ISS-0421 regression: the 6 gated sweeps' max_concurrency derives live from Admission.global_cap/0, not a hardcoded literal', 1 test -- global_cap forced to 1 (pool_size:3/reserved_headroom:2), 5 schemas' due timers (wider margin than REQ-218 AC2's own 3) all fire within a single tick. Deterministic in both directions: with the live accessor (max_concurrency==1, no self-contention) all 5 succeed; with a hardcoded value >1 racing the same sole global_cap==1 unit, strictly fewer than 5 would fire (Admission grants exactly one, never retries the rest).

3. NEW GAP FOUND (AC1 fault isolation -- no existing test exercised the actual NEW mechanism): every existing fault-isolation test (REQ-218 AC5, ISS-0444's 3 describes) exercises either a pre-existing inline rescue or Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1's/run_retention_sweep/1's own internal Postgrex :undefined_table/:undefined_schema rescue (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex) -- NOT the NEW top-level try/rescue this fix's design Sec4b adds at the poll_and_fire/retention_sweep Task.async_stream call sites specifically. Closed by describe 'ISS-0421 AC1: new top-level per-task rescue', 1 test: drops the fire_at column from one schema's timers table (Postgrex :undefined_column, a code NOT in poll_and_fire/1's own rescue's matched list), forcing a raise that reaches poller.ex's NEW rescue for the first time in this suite. Asserts the tick doesn't crash, a different healthy schema's own poll_and_fire still completes in the same tick, and the log line is the NEW rescue's own ('poller sweep task raised' from log_task_raise/4), not the pre-existing Scheduler-level 'tenant schema unavailable' line.

4. NEW GAP FOUND (AC4 single-query-per-tick -- unchanged property, never itself encoded as an automated invariant): closed by describe 'ISS-0421 AC4: tenant_schemas/0 is still queried exactly once per tick', 1 test -- reads poller.ex's own source text, isolates handle_info(:tick, state)'s body, asserts the substring 'fetch_tenant_schemas()' occurs exactly once inside it. Mirrors the existing 'no second ticker' (use GenServer grep) and REQ-218 AC4 ({:tenant, grep) tests' own established idiom.

5. AC3 (peak DBConnection checkouts stated/justified) traceability: no new test needed -- AC3 is the arithmetic identity design Sec3a/3b/3c states, already pinned down by (a) global_cap/1's new tests (item 1) at multiple non-default configs, (b) the pre-existing AdmissionTest 'AC1: global cap = pool_size - reserved_headroom' block proving try_acquire(:global) itself enforces that derived number, (c) item 2's mutation-verified test tying max_concurrency to that same live number for the 6 gated sweeps, and (d) reserved_headroom/1's own existing REQ-218-era coverage for the one unwrapped sweep's half of the identity. No additional runtime test would exercise anything these don't already cover.

MUTATION-TESTED EVERY NEW TEST MYSELF (foreground, all reverted and confirmed clean via `diff`/`git diff --stat` afterward):
- global_cap/1 tests: hardcoded handle_call(:global_cap, ...) to reply a fixed 8 regardless of state.global_cap -> `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs`: 16/18 passed, exactly the 2 non-default-value tests (items a/b above) failed as expected (the default-config test (c) could not distinguish live-read from a same-valued hardcode by construction -- expected, not a gap). Reverted, re-ran: 18/18 passed.
- Hardcoded-literal regression test: sed-replaced `Admission.global_cap()` with the literal `8` at all 6 call sites in poller.ex (the exact mutation REVIEWER/ELIXIR-DEV each performed by hand at step-04d) -> `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: 15/19 passed, 4 failed -- this new test PLUS the same 3 REQ-218 tests (AC1, AC2, AC5) REVIEWER's own manual pass already named (the antagonist-based AC3 test did not happen to fail this particular run, consistent with its own documented nondeterminism -- it is not the test this regression targets). Reverted, re-ran: 19/19 passed.
- AC1 rescue test: removed the try/rescue wrapper around the poll_and_fire call site (reverting that one call site to its pre-fix shape) -> `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: 18/19 passed, exactly 1 failure -- this new AC1 test, and no other. Reverted, re-ran: 19/19 passed.
All reverts confirmed clean via `git diff --stat lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex lib/letflow/admission.ex` producing no output (byte-identical to the committed pre-mutation state).

TEST RUN NUMBERS (foreground, real output, this run):
- `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: Result: 37 passed, exit 0.
- `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs`: Result: 57 passed, exit 0.
- `mix letflow.check.test` (full suite, forces fresh warnings-as-errors recompile, greps for the ISS-0069 dead-default-argument substring), run to completion in the foreground (~1616s): `Result: 3212/3214 passed (6/6 properties, 3206/3208 tests), 21 excluded, Failed: 2 tests`. The 2 failures are both `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` 'rust pin (REQ-165)' tests (`test rust pin (REQ-165) a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row naming expected and running`, `test rust pin (REQ-165) a matching rust pin reports OK with no mismatch`) -- the same pre-existing rustc-not-on-PATH sandbox gap REVIEWER's own step-04d run and this run's own earlier REQ-217/REQ-218 specs already document, confirmed by name, zero relation to this diff. `grep -c "default values for the optional arguments" /tmp/check_test_full.log` == 0 -- the ISS-0069 target substring does not occur anywhere in the captured output. The task's own exit code is nonzero (1) solely because of its documented contract ('exits 1 if the subprocess exited nonzero, regardless of the substring check') given the 2 pre-existing rustc failures -- not because of any new test failure or the substring it actually gates on.

No skipped/pending tests introduced. All new tests are deterministic (no wall-clock or unseeded-randomness dependence) except where they reuse this codebase's own already-established deterministic-hold idioms.
